Over three different solvent campaigns, ION operated for over 7500 hours on a flue gas slipstream from a market-adaptive NGCC gas turbine (4-5.2% CO ). 2 The campaign began with 250 hours of parametric testing with MEA to baseline the system with an industry standard solvent. ION achieved capture efficiencies as high as 89% and captured 76 tCO 2 with MEA. ION performed 350 hours of parametric testing with its ICE-21™ solvent and this was followed by 817 hours of long-term testing. ION achieved capture efficiencies up to 99% with ICE-21™. ION performed over 2250 hours of parametric testing and nearly 4000 hours of long-term testing with ICE-31®, capturing ~2500 tCO . ION demonstrated capture efficiencies as high as 99.4% with 2 ICE-31®, at which point the outlet flue gas contains a lower concentration of CO than ambient air 2 (~400 ppm). ICE-31® demonstrated excellent solvent stability in the high-oxygen environment that results from the combustion of NGCC flue gas. This was further shown through the extremely low emissions of ICE-31®. Project Enterprise showcased the exceptional qualities of ION capture solvents and demonstrated ION’s deep understanding of amine-based carbon capture and ability to apply that knowledge in a functioning industrial setting. The results confirm and expand ION’s expectations that ICE-31® is an exceptional solvent for flue gases with high oxidative potential, such as NGCC facilities like LMEC. The results from the ENTP pilot further demonstrate the readiness of ICE-31® as a viable, commercially deployable carbon capture technology.
